rows.note: This is the all-purpose spoken choice for a continuing minor pain or ache.

example.english: I still have a slight ache in my head.
example.jyutping: ngo5 go3 tau4 zung6 jau5 siu2 siu2 tung3

rows.note: Use this for an aching or sore feeling, especially in muscles, joints, or limbs.

example.english: After exercising, there is still an ache in my legs.
example.traditional: 做完運動，我對腳仲有啲酸痛。
example.jyutping: zou6 jyun4 wan6 dung6 ngo5 deoi3 goek3 zung6 jau5 di1 syun1 tung3

rows.note: Use this when you specifically want to contrast a dull, lingering pain with a sharp or spasmodic one.

example.english: This kind of dull ache is different from a sharp pain.
example.jyutping: nei1 zung2 jan2 tung3 tung4 ci3 tung3 m4 tung4

rows.note: This is the all-purpose verb phrase for saying that someone feels or suffers pain.

example.english: I have a bit of an ache in my head.
example.jyutping: ngo5 gok3 dak1 go3 tau4 jau5 di1 tung3

rows.note: Use this for a persistent, dull ache, especially in a body part, wound, or internal area.

example.english: My old injury still has a dull ache.
example.jyutping: ngo5 ge3 gau6 waan6 zung6 jan2 jan2 zok3 tung3

rows.note: Use this causative construction when something is the source of another person's or body part's pain.

example.english: These new shoes make my feet ache.
example.traditional: 呢對新鞋搞到我對腳好痛。
example.jyutping: ni1 deoi3 san1 haai4 gaau2 dou3 ngo5 deoi3 goek3 hou2 tung3
